The ratio of the image height to the object height is equal to the ratio of the image distance to the object distance: $\frac{h_i}{h_o} = \frac{d_i}{d_o}$. If the object distance is reduced by half ($d_o$ becomes $\frac{1}{2}d_o$), the denominator of the ratio decreases by a factor of 2, which causes the resulting image size to increase by a factor of 2. Therefore, the image is double the original size.
